text: The water hisses and turns to steam where your spell lands. The river shrugs and keeps flowing.
Bright light on the water. Very pretty. Still very wet.
The blade dips into the current and is gone. The river does not care about edges.
The river takes your spell and keeps going. It has been doing this for a long time.
The door is now wet and just as closed. The joke is still not funny.
A green shoot curls around the hinge. It is charming. It does not open the door.
The door is unmoved. Even the joke on it looks smug.
The bramble is now damp and even more stubborn.
A rock lands on the bramble and now you have a rock and a bramble.
The bramble closes ranks. Now it looks personal.
You drop stones in. Now the garden is wet and has stones in it.
The boat is lovely. It does not remove any water.
The water sits there, patient as ever. The frog is still winning.
The wind pushes at the water. The water pushes back. Nothing is crossed.
You reach for a stone. It rolls away again, almost apologetically.
The current rolls on, unimpressed. Your boots are already wet.
A warm glow on the sand. The boat is not moved, but it is now cosy.
The shallows freeze. Now the boat is high on ice instead of sand.
The boat stays exactly where it was, and the sea stays exactly where it is.
The snow is now wet snow. You have made the problem heavier.
A branch sticks out of a drift. It is a start, not a road.
The snow absorbs the effort and gives nothing back.
The ground is now nicely lit by nothing at all. You are still in the dark.
A blade glints faintly. Then it stops glinting. Then it is dark again.
Darkness answers darkness. Nothing else happens.
The stones get wet. The pass is still blocked, but cleaner.
A tree grows beside the rockfall. Nice shade. No path.
The rockfall shifts by a finger's width and settles again.
Your flame gutters in the rain. The storm is not impressed.
A boat on a road. Even the storm pauses to judge you.
The storm notices you, which is worse than being ignored.
The branches are wet now. Heavier, too.
Snow on a wreck. It is beautiful. It is still a wreck.
The tangle creaks, settles, and keeps the road closed.
Water runs down the rock. The rock is now slippery and still tall.
The rock glows warm. It is a warm wall. You are still below it.
The ridge looks down at you. It has done this to better climbers.
The field is now warm and even drier. The crow is disappointed.
A blade cuts a neat line in the dust. Nothing grows along it.
The field waits. It has waited longer than this.
You drop stones in the street. The water is higher and now there are stones.
Something small swims past. It is having a lovely time. The street is still flooded.
The water finds your shoes and stays there, delighted.
The gate is wet. The orchard is still on the other side.
The gate is now cold and just as shut.
The gate holds. The orchard keeps its secret.
A splash on bronze. The bell stays quiet.
A stone bounces off the bell with a dull thud. The village winces.
The bronze swallows the sound and offers nothing back.
The village gets darker and sleeps even more deeply.
A cold snap. Everyone pulls the blankets tighter.
The village sleeps on. Somewhere the cat sighs.
The water below is beautiful. It is also very far down.
The gorge takes your spell and gives back an echo.
The chest is damp and still locked.
The chest rattles once, smugly, and stays shut.
A flame in a crowded market is a bad idea. The crowd moves away from you, not for you.
The crowd shifts, closes, and carries on its business.
The ice thins. Warm, but unhelpful.
The ice creaks under your feet and declines to help.
The wall is wet. The wall is still tall.
The wall keeps its apples and its silence.
The wind pushes the cart deeper. The merchant is not grateful.
The cart digs in deeper. The ox looks embarrassed for you.
You make the dark darker. Very impressive. Very unhelpful.
The dark is generous. It gives you more dark.
The dragon wakes a little, sighs a warm breath, and goes back to sleep. You are now warm.
The dragon stirs, sighs out a warm breath, and sleeps on.
The desert is now hotter. The bird looks personally let down.
The sand takes your spell and returns heat.
A stone thuds against the bronze. The village winces.
The bell hangs there, enormous and uninterested.
The snow turns to slush. Every step is heavier now.
The drift settles into a new shape and stays in the way.
A flame in a storm. The rain puts it out and the boat stays out.
The storm throws your spell back at the shore.
The wheel is not turning for heat. Find something that pushes it.
Ice would stop the wheel, not start it. Think about what moves water or air.
The lanterns are not going to light from water. Something warm or bright is needed.
Cold will not light a path. Try something that brings light or warmth.
The frost is too thick for a little heat. Try something gentler and wider.
Water would only freeze again here. Something dry and bright is needed.
